name: Hexarelin
used_for: A synthetic growth hormone secretagogue that acts on the ghrelin receptor. It has no approved medical use in the US and no FDA label. It is promoted online for muscle, fat loss, recovery and heart protection. Human research is limited to small, short studies from the late 1990s and 2000s (hormone responses in healthy volunteers and acute heart-function studies); the heart-protection findings mostly come from animals.

entries.text: 1.5 micrograms per kg subcutaneously two or three times in one day, then 1 microgram per kg intravenously at the end of each 24-hour sampling period. Single-day exposure only.
Four doses of 50 micrograms at hourly intervals from 22:00 to 01:00 versus placebo (the route is not stated in the abstract).
A single intravenous dose of 2.0 micrograms per kg during bypass surgery.
Animal study only, not human data: 0.3 mg per kg per day for 21 days after induced heart attack.

internet_entries.text: An educational website (PeptidesExplorer) says typical use is 100 to 200 mcg subcutaneously once or twice daily on an empty stomach, with 100 mcg once daily described as conservative and 200 mcg once or twice daily as standard.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: The Peptides Insider website says hexarelin works best fasted, with no food for about 2 hours before and 30 minutes after, taken in the morning, before a workout or at bedtime, and that a mixed vial is kept at 2 to 8 C, protected from light and used within about 28 days. The site carries affiliate links to sellers.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A rejuvenation clinic page (Wittmer Rejuvenation Clinic) says hexarelin is injected at bedtime, that it does not need to be taken on an empty stomach, and that the mixed vial is kept refrigerated with injection sites rotated.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: After four hexarelin injections during the evening in seven healthy volunteers, deep (stage 4) sleep and EEG delta power decreased, and the authors suggested sleep was impaired; GH, prolactin, ACTH and cortisol increased.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: With repeated daily subcutaneous hexarelin, the GH response to a later intravenous test dose was blunted and the ACTH and cortisol responses were abolished, indicating down-regulation.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Intravenous hexarelin raised mean arterial pressure in patients with coronary artery disease under anesthesia, alongside increases in ejection fraction and cardiac output.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A telehealth company's article says hexarelin is marketed for energy, muscle, recovery and body composition, but argues the research is limited and does not support most of those claims, and says its sleep study showed less deep sleep and higher cortisol.

A sports-medicine clinic's peptide library page presents hexarelin as promoting lean muscle, fat metabolism, cardiovascular function and anti-inflammatory effects, and invites readers to book a consultation.

research.summary: Six healthy young men received hexarelin by subcutaneous injection two or three times in a day, with 24-hour blood sampling (Eur J Endocrinol).
research.finding: Growth hormone output rose to the same extent with two or three injections, and a later intravenous dose produced a blunted growth hormone response, which fits desensitization. IGF-I did not change after this one-day schedule. Tiny, one-day study.

research.summary: Placebo-controlled study of hexarelin during sleep in seven healthy young volunteers (Psychoneuroendocrinology).
research.finding: Hexarelin raised growth hormone, prolactin, ACTH and cortisol, and reduced deep (stage 4) sleep and delta-wave activity, so sleep was worse after the peptide. Very small study.

research.summary: Comparison of intravenous hexarelin and GHRP-2 with GHRH in six young and six elderly healthy people (Peptides).
research.finding: Hexarelin and GHRP-2 produced similar, strong growth hormone responses, larger than GHRH, but also raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol, so the effect is not specific to growth hormone.

research.summary: Randomized comparison of single intravenous hexarelin, GHRH, growth hormone or placebo in 24 men with coronary artery disease during bypass surgery (Eur J Pharmacol).
research.finding: Hexarelin transiently increased ejection fraction and cardiac output for up to 90 minutes and raised mean arterial pressure, while the other agents did not. These are acute measurements under anesthesia, not evidence of treatment benefit.

research.summary: Acute intravenous hexarelin in 13 patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction, compared with healthy and growth-hormone-deficient people (Eur J Heart Fail).
research.finding: Ejection fraction rose in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy but not in those with dilated cardiomyopathy, despite similar growth hormone release. Small, acute study.

research.summary: Cell-culture study of the ghrelin receptor exposed to hexarelin (J Endocrinol Invest).
research.finding: The cells' calcium response to hexarelin faded within minutes of the first dose, showing rapid receptor desensitization. Cell-culture evidence only.

research.summary: Mouse heart-attack model treated with hexarelin or vehicle for 21 days (Physiol Rep).
research.finding: Treated mice had better heart function and less scarring than vehicle mice. Findings in mice do not show the same effect in people.

research.summary: Study in 7 healthy young adults of how an oral glucose load and arginine change the growth hormone response to injected GHRH (Ghigo et al., Metabolism).
research.finding: Oral glucose beforehand lowered the GH peak after GHRH from 11.6 to 7.4 micrograms per liter; the authors suggest, from indirect evidence, that glucose acts by raising hypothalamic somatostatin.

research.summary: Frequent-sampling study of 24-hour growth hormone secretion in 6 healthy men on a fed day and on days 1 and 5 of a 5-day fast (Ho et al., J Clin Invest).
research.finding: Fasting increased growth hormone secretion and amplified its daily rhythms compared with the fed day.

research.summary: Study of growth hormone secretion in healthy men in relation to sleep and time of day, using deconvolution of frequent blood samples (Van Cauter et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: A GH pulse began within 30 minutes of sleep onset in every profile with normal sleep, and about 70% of pulses during sleep were tied to slow-wave sleep.

dose.summary: Not approved. Studies used about 1 to 2 micrograms per kg, or 50 mcg doses hourly at night. Online sources describe 100 to 200 mcg, with one clinic describing 0.2 mg.

timing.summary: One study found evening doses reduced deep sleep. Online sources disagree: some say morning, others bedtime, and none cite a trial of dose timing.

items.text: The body's own largest growth hormone (GH) pulse comes shortly after falling asleep, during deep sleep. This is natural GH, not hexarelin, and no trial has compared bedtime with daytime hexarelin dosing.
items.label: research

fasting.summary: No study tested food with hexarelin. Online sources mostly say to inject on an empty stomach, based on glucose blunting GH in studies of other compounds, while one clinic says it is not needed.

items.text: In healthy adults, a glucose drink before an injection of natural growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) lowered the GH response by about a third; the authors suggest somatostatin as the reason. Hexarelin acts differently, and no study has tested meals with it.
items.label: research
